# Erdős Problem 109

@[expose] public section

open Pointwise

namespace Erdos109

/--
Any $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains a sumset $B+C$ where both $B$ and $C$
are infinite.

The Erdős sumset conjecture. Proved by Moreira, Richter, and Robertson [MRR19].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos109.lean#L9074"]
theorem erdos_109 (A : Set ℕ) (h : A.upperDensity > 0) :
    ∃ B C : Set ℕ, B.Infinite ∧ C.Infinite ∧ B + C ⊆ A := by
  sorry

end Erdos109

reformulations.difference: The Lean uses Lean's ℕ (which contains 0) for A, B and C, and measures upper density with Set.upperDensity = limsup_{b→∞} |A ∩ [0,b)| / b. The source (MRR Conjecture 1.1; erdosproblems.com/109) takes ℕ = {1,2,...} and upper density limsup_{N→∞} |A ∩ {1,…,N}| / N. So B or C may contain 0 in the Lean statement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (Lean ⇒ source) Take A ⊆ {1,2,...} with limsup |A∩{1..N}|/N > 0. Then |A∩{1..N}| ≤ |A∩[0,N+1)|, so the source ratio is at most 2·partialDensity(N+1) for N ≥ 1, and A.upperDensity > 0. The Lean statement gives infinite B, C with B + C ⊆ A. Then B\{0} and C\{0} are still infinite, avoid 0, and (B\{0})+(C\{0}) ⊆ B + C ⊆ A. (source ⇒ Lean) Take A with A.upperDensity > 0 and put A' = A\{0}. Since |A∩[0,N)| ≤ |A'∩{1..N}| + 1, the source ratio for A' is at least partialDensity_A(N) − 1/N, so A' has positive upper density in the source's sense. The source gives B, C ⊆ {1,2,...} infinite with B + C ⊆ A' ⊆ A. Both partial-density sequences are bounded, so Lean's limsup on ℝ is the usual one. I proved `LeanStatement ↔ SrcStatement` in /workspace/review/equiv.lean (theorem Review.equiv; axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only).

review.notes: The file has one declaration, Erdos109.erdos_109. Printing its elaborated form confirms it is `Set.upperDensity A Set.univ > 0 → ∃ B C, B.Infinite ∧ C.Infinite ∧ B + C ⊆ A`, where `+` is the pointwise sumset `Set.add` (`⊆` shows up as `Set.instLE`'s `≤` under pp.explicit) and the existential uses `∧`, not `→`. Set.upperDensity is the limsup on ℝ of |A ∩ [0,b)|/b. These values lie in [0,1], so no default value is involved. Checked in Lean: univ ↦ 1, even numbers ↦ 1/2, finite sets ↦ 0. The docstring matches erdosproblems.com/109 word for word: 'Any A ⊆ ℕ of positive upper density contains a sumset B+C where both B and C are infinite. … Proved by Moreira, Richter, and Robertson [MRR19].' It also matches MRR's Conjecture 1.1. Status: `research solved` matches the site's PROVED and the teorth database's 'proved (Lean)'. The formal_proof link resolves to a theorem with an identical statement (line 9074). It imports a copy of the same Set.partialDensity/Set.upperDensity definitions (Util/Density.lean) and contains no sorry or axiom. I could not run that proof, since it targets a different Lean/Mathlib version. The live erdosproblems.com page was blocked by Cloudflare, so I used the Wayback snapshot of 2026-07-14; the page was last edited 27 September 2025. I did not read the original Erdős–Graham 1980 text [ErGr80, p.85]. The file does not cite it, and the sources it does cite settle the statement.
